lines: // One concurrency limiter per tenant (System.Threading.RateLimiting): 5 permits, no queue
// POST /orders: A's storm can't drain B's capacity
if (!lease.IsAcquired)   // the tenant's 5 permits are taken
// ... create the order while the lease is held
ops._why: examples/12 per-tenant bulkhead on its library (S14); the slide is an excerpt

paragraphs: The bulkhead comes from System.Threading.RateLimiting, which is in the box: a PartitionedRateLimiter keyed by tenant, with one ConcurrencyLimiter per partition, five permits and a queue limit of zero. The endpoint takes a lease for the order's tenant; a tenant that already has five orders in flight gets a lease that is not acquired, and the request is answered with 429 at once while every other tenant keeps its own five.

The same library drives the ASP.NET Core rate-limiting middleware, but the middleware chooses its partition before the request body is read, and the tenant arrives in the body, so the endpoint takes the lease itself. Polly's AddConcurrencyLimiter wraps the same limiter for outbound calls. At the platform layer, Istio connection-pool limits per destination complement these in-process limits.
